title: Fatal accident — 60-ton dumper crossed dump-edge berm and overturned, Kusmunda OC
summary: A 60-ton dumper at Kusmunda Opencast Mine (SECL, Korba) crossed the berm at the Rehandling OB dump edge during dumping and overturned; the operator died on the spot. This is the real DGMS Safety Alert 23/2026, ingested as the source PDF for the scenario.
paragraphs: It has come to the notice of the Directorate General of Mines Safety that a fatal accident occurred at Kusmunda Opencast Mine (M/s SECL, Korba, Chhattisgarh) on 21.06.2026 at about 12:45 AM (C shift). A 60-ton dumper, while carrying out dumping at the Rehandling OB dump, crossed the berm at the dumping edge and fell down. The vehicle overturned; the dumper operator, Shri Satyanarayan, sustained fatal injuries and succumbed on the spot.
Preliminary inquiry indicates the dumper was operating at the dumping edge without a demarcated safe operating limit; the edge berm failed to arrest the vehicle before it crossed the edge.

All opencast mines with HEMM fleets and overburden-dumping operations are directed to: (a) maintain a safe distance from the dump edge and enforce a clearly demarcated safe operating limit; (b) construct and regularly inspect stop-blocks, berms or safety bunds of adequate height and strength along all dump edges; (c) permit only trained, competent and authorized operators for dump-edge operations, with special training on dump-edge operations, machine controls, blind spots and emergency response; (d) enforce seat-belt usage on all mobile equipment.
These precautions shall be implemented within 7 days of the issue of this alert and evidence of compliance shall be maintained at the mine for inspection.

title: Slope stability monitoring protocol for high-wall benches above 30 m
summary: Technical circular mandating continuous slope monitoring on high-wall benches above 30 m — extensometer, prism survey and slope-stability radar thresholds.
paragraphs: DGMS Technical Circular 27/2026 directs all opencast mines with high-wall benches exceeding 30 m in height to maintain continuous slope stability monitoring.
Monitoring shall comprise in-situ extensometer/MPBX arrays, periodic prism surveys, and where available slope-stability radar coverage on active benches.
An alarm shall be raised when measured displacement exceeds 2.5 mm per day or crack width increases beyond the geotechnical assessment threshold.
Weekly displacement reports shall be submitted to the Regional Inspector and retained at the mine.

title: Safety parameter deviation — PPE non-compliance flagged for Shovel Crew B
summary: CIL Safety Information System flagged a PPE-compliance deviation: workers on Shovel Crew B without ISI-marked footwear during the last safety-parameter audit.
paragraphs: The CIL Safety Information System (CSIS) recorded a deviation during the routine safety-parameter audit of Shovel Crew B (MINE-002).
18 workers were observed on the shovel bench without ISI 15298-marked safety footwear; two helmet chin-straps were found defective.
Corrective action: issue replacement PPE, update the PPE issuance register, and re-audit within 7 days under the Mines Rules, 1955 (safety apparel provisions).

title: Strata displacement anomaly — Bench-1 extensometer, MINE-004
summary: Extensometer EX-07 on Bench-1 (subsidence zone) recorded 3.1 mm/24 h displacement — above the 2.5 mm geotechnical threshold.
paragraphs: Telemetry from extensometer EX-07 (Bench-1, MINE-004 subsidence zone) reported a 24-hour displacement of 3.1 mm against a 2.5 mm geotechnical threshold.
Prism pair PR-12 shows a correlated vector shift of 1.9 mm toward the pit, consistent with progressive creep rather than blasting vibration.
Immediate action: ground-truth the reading, review the geotechnical assessment, and verify the telemetry link per the slope-stability monitoring protocol in DGMS Tech. Circular 27/2026.

title: PM10 exceedance at Haul Road #4 ambient monitoring station
summary: State Pollution Control Board monitoring station at Haul Road #4 recorded 168 µg/m³ PM10 (24-h avg) against the 100 µg/m³ standard — an EC Condition 14 breach.
paragraphs: The ambient air quality station at Haul Road #4 (MINE-003) recorded a 24-hour average PM10 of 168 µg/m³ against the 100 µg/m³ standard under EC Condition 14.
High readings coincide with gaps in water-sprinkler coverage during dry-shift haulage and stockpile handling.
Intensify dust suppression, verify sprinkler nozzle calibration, and report corrective action to the State Pollution Control Board within 7 days.

title: Satellite detection — vegetation loss in no-mining buffer, MINE-002
summary: Coal Mine Surveillance and Management System satellite imagery shows an 18% NDVI drop in the western no-mining buffer of MINE-002.
paragraphs: CMSMS satellite monitoring flagged an 18% negative NDVI change in the western buffer zone of MINE-002 over the last two survey cycles.
Change classification indicates vegetation loss rather than seasonal variation; possible boundary encroachment or overburden spill needs ground verification.
Conduct a ground-truth survey, re-verify boundary pegs against the approved mine plan, and submit findings with geo-tagged evidence.
